name: GRAPHITE
summary: A Dragos-designated Stage 1 OT threat group conducting credential theft and espionage against energy, logistics and industrial organisations, with reported overlap to APT28.
primaryFocus: Industrial-sector credential access, reconnaissance and persistent intelligence collection

stateAffiliation.assessment: The Russia nexus is derived from Dragos's reported technical overlap with APT28 and corroborating reporting on APT28 infrastructure; Dragos does not make political attribution for the GRAPHITE cluster itself.

observedSince.label: GRAPHITE activity cluster
observedSince.qualification: Dragos currently dates the public GRAPHITE profile from 2023 while describing campaigns since 2022.

observedSince.label: Underlying campaign activity
observedSince.qualification: Dragos reports spearphishing and credential-focused operations since 2022.

designations.name: GRAPHITE
designations.description: The primary industrial threat activity cluster described in this dossier.

designations.name: APT28
designations.description: A broader Russian military intelligence cluster reported by Dragos as overlapping GRAPHITE.

designations.name: Forest Blizzard
designations.description: Microsoft's designation for APT28 activity; included as provider context rather than a direct GRAPHITE alias.

designations.name: GRU Military Unit 26165
designations.description: Government attribution scope for the APT28-operated EdgeRouter botnet disrupted in 2024.

assessment.text: GRAPHITE is positioned in Stage 1 of the ICS Cyber Kill Chain: it steals credentials, inventories targets and maintains access, but Dragos has not reported disruptive ICS effects for this cluster.

The group has exploited high-value client vulnerabilities, used compromised Ubiquiti EdgeRouters and shifted towards legitimate internet services and code-hosting platforms after the 2024 botnet disruption.

GRAPHITE's industrial relevance is preparatory: credential capture and intelligence collection can enable later operations, but evidence should not be inflated into an unobserved process-manipulation capability.

regions.name: West Asia and the Middle East

technologies.name: Legitimate API testing and code-hosting services

campaigns.name: Industrial credential-theft campaigns
campaigns.summary: Targeted spearphishing and exploitation collected credentials from energy, logistics and industrial organisations connected to the conflict in Ukraine.
campaigns.impact: Persistent access and intelligence collection can expose industrial network knowledge and create options for follow-on operations.

campaigns.name: Compromised EdgeRouter infrastructure
campaigns.summary: Compromised Ubiquiti EdgeRouters were used to distribute malware and conceal command-and-control activity; a U.S.-led operation disrupted an APT28-operated botnet in January 2024.
campaigns.impact: Third-party router infrastructure obscured attribution and separated actor traffic from direct command infrastructure.

campaigns.name: Post-takedown legitimate-service staging
campaigns.summary: Following the router-botnet disruption, GRAPHITE shifted staging and delivery towards legitimate internet services, API testing platforms and GitHub.
campaigns.impact: Abuse of trusted services reduces the value of domain-only blocking and demands behavioural monitoring.

capabilities.name: Exploit client and edge vulnerabilities
capabilities.description: Use high-impact vulnerabilities, including no-click Outlook credential theft, to acquire access and authentication material.

capabilities.name: Steal credentials and conduct reconnaissance
capabilities.description: Collect identity material and information about industrial targets without publicly observed process disruption.

capabilities.name: Operate through compromised routers and legitimate services
capabilities.description: Relay traffic through SOHO routers and stage payloads through trusted web services.

malware.name: OCEANMAP
malware.description: One of several custom capabilities Dragos associates with GRAPHITE operations.

malware.name: HEADLACE / MASEPIE / STEELHOOK
malware.description: Custom payload families named by Dragos in the public GRAPHITE capability set.

enterprise.name: Phishing: Spearphishing Attachment
enterprise.behaviour: Targeted attachments and lures supported access to organisations linked to Ukraine.

enterprise.name: Forced Authentication
enterprise.behaviour: CVE-2023-23397 caused Outlook clients to send Net-NTLMv2 material to actor-controlled infrastructure without user interaction.

enterprise.name: Exploitation for Client Execution
enterprise.behaviour: Client-side vulnerabilities were used to gain code execution or credential access.

enterprise.name: Compromise Infrastructure: Network Devices
enterprise.behaviour: Compromised Ubiquiti EdgeRouters provided relay and concealment infrastructure.

ics.name: Spearphishing Attachment
ics.behaviour: Industrial-sector spearphishing is mapped as a Stage 1 access path; no ICS process effect is asserted.

ics.name: External Remote Services
ics.behaviour: Captured credentials and external access services create a route towards industrial environments.

ics.name: Internet Accessible Device
ics.behaviour: The public record emphasises internet-facing edge infrastructure and industrial organisations rather than direct controller manipulation.

indicatorNotice: No point-in-time indicators are published in this dossier. Router, hosting and legitimate-service infrastructure is shared and dynamic; hunt the access chain and credential behaviour instead of blocking broad provider ranges.

defensivePriorities.name: Patch credential-leaking client flaws
defensivePriorities.description: Prioritise Outlook CVE-2023-23397 remediation and restrict outbound SMB to untrusted networks.

defensivePriorities.name: Protect and monitor edge routers
defensivePriorities.description: Remove default credentials, update SOHO/edge devices and alert on unexplained administrative scripts or firewall changes.

defensivePriorities.name: Detect credential replay
defensivePriorities.description: Correlate new remote access, mailbox permission changes and authentication from relay infrastructure after suspected credential capture.

defensivePriorities.name: Constrain legitimate-service abuse
defensivePriorities.description: Inspect payload retrieval and unusual automation involving API testing, code hosting and newly introduced web services.
